# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 64

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 10

---

## Disagreement 1 — 64:1 "grievous appearance" vs. "downcast appearance"

- **EMET:** "grievous appearance"
- **LOGOS:** "downcast appearance"
- **PNEUMA:** "grim expression"
- **Greek:** *phaulos* — mean/bad/paltry/downcast (range of meanings)
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "downcast appearance" (LOGOS). *Phaulos* in this aesthetic context means inferior/mean in appearance; "downcast" captures the visual impression; "grievous" (EMET) overloads the adjective emotionally.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 64:2 "beguiling them with evil desires" vs. "luring them with evil desires"

- **EMET:** "beguiling them with evil desires in which they shall perish"
- **LOGOS:** "beguiling them with evil desires in which they shall perish"
- **PNEUMA:** "luring them with evil desires that bring them to ruin"
- **Note:** EMET and LOGOS agree.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "beguiling them with evil desires in which they shall perish." "Beguiling" (*apatōn*) carries the seductive deception sense; "luring" (PNEUMA) is simpler but slightly less precise.

---

## Disagreement 3 — 64:2 "vain deceptions" vs. "empty delusions"

- **EMET:** "walk in vain deceptions and arrogances"
- **LOGOS:** "walk in vain deceptions and the pride of this life"
- **PNEUMA:** "live in empty delusions and the arrogance of this present life"
- **Greek:** *en tais apotais kenais kai en tais alazoneiias tou biou toutou* — in empty/vain deceptions and in the arrogances of this life
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "walk in vain deceptions and the pride of this life" (LOGOS). *Kenais apatais* = empty/vain deceptions; *alazoneia* = arrogance/boastfulness/pride; LOGOS preserves both well.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 64:2 "some unto death, and some unto the corruption of their lives"

- **EMET:** "some unto death, and some unto the corruption of their lives"
- **LOGOS:** "some to death, others to the corruption of their lives"
- **PNEUMA:** "some completely, others by corrupting their way of living"
- **Note:** EMET and LOGOS agree on substance.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "some to death, others to the corruption of their lives" (LOGOS). The two-tier destruction is important; PNEUMA's "completely" for "to death" loses the eschatological weight.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 64:3 "when a desire comes upon any of the servants of God" vs. "when any of the servants entertains a desire"

- **EMET:** "when a desire comes upon any of the servants of God"
- **LOGOS:** "when any of the servants of God entertains a desire"
- **PNEUMA:** "whenever any of God's servants develops a craving"
- **Greek:** *hotan tis epithumēsē* — when any person desires/craves
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "when any of the servants of God entertains a desire" (LOGOS). "Entertains a desire" captures the deliberate dwelling on the desire; PNEUMA's "craving" adds intensity.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 64:3 "fills the man's heart with great desires" — all agree substantially

- **EMET:** "fills the man's heart with great desires"
- **LOGOS:** "fills the man's heart with great desires"
- **PNEUMA:** "fills their heart with powerful cravings"
- **Note:** Minor variation.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "fills the man's heart with great desires" (EMET/LOGOS). "Great desires" preserves the scale (*megalas epithumias*).

---

## Disagreement 7 — 64:3 "implanting vain pleasures" vs. "implanting empty pleasures"

- **EMET:** "implanting vain pleasures"
- **LOGOS:** "implanting empty pleasures"
- **PNEUMA:** "implants hollow pleasures in them"
- **Greek:** *enempipletai hēdonas kenas* — fills/implants empty pleasures
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "implanting empty pleasures" (LOGOS). *Kenas* = empty/hollow; "empty" is more literal than "vain"; "hollow" (PNEUMA) is an acceptable synonym.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 64:3 "great blindness" vs. "spiritual blindness"

- **EMET:** "he is filled with great blindness for what he has done"
- **LOGOS:** "he is filled with great blindness regarding what he has done"
- **PNEUMA:** "they are overtaken by great spiritual blindness"
- **Greek:** *plēsthēsetai megas tuphlosin* — filled with great blindness
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "he is filled with great blindness regarding what he has done" (LOGOS). PNEUMA's "spiritual" is an interpretive addition; the blindness is about moral self-assessment, not spiritual sight per se.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 64:4 "seem to be righteous" vs. "seem righteous in his own eyes"

- **EMET:** "certain deeds seem to be righteous"
- **LOGOS:** "certain things seem righteous in his own eyes"
- **PNEUMA:** "certain things look righteous in their own eyes"
- **Greek:** *dokeī dikaia einai* — seems to be righteous
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "certain things seem righteous in his own eyes" (LOGOS). Adding "in his own eyes" makes explicit what is implicit — the person's subjective assessment differs from God's.

---

## Disagreement 10 — 64:4 "reckoned as sins" vs. "are sins"

- **EMET:** "in the sight of the Lord they are sins"
- **LOGOS:** "in the sight of the Lord they are reckoned as sins"
- **PNEUMA:** "are reckoned as sins by the Lord"
- **Greek:** *enōpion tou kyriou hamartiai eisin* — before/in sight of the Lord they are sins
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "in the sight of the Lord they are reckoned as sins" (LOGOS). "Reckoned as sins" preserves the accounting/juridical dimension (*logizomai*) while EMET's "are sins" is blunter.

---

*End of disagreement log for Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 64.*
